ambiguities.description: Table 1 and Sec. 2.2 give 1.45 %; the Fig. 5 identified curve peaks at 2.574e-6 m/N (= 1/(2*0.0145*1.34e7)). But the Fig. 6a uncontrolled peak (-111.10 dB -> 1.339 %), the Fig. 6b open-loop pole (-10.89 +- 812.2j rad/s -> 1.341 %) and the uncontrolled SLD minima (1.212 mm; model with 1.34 %: 1.213 mm) all imply 1.34 %. The computed curves of the paper use 1.34 %.
Text: gains between 237 and 1487 V s/m. Fig. 8 maximum 1487 (740 rpm) agrees, but the Fig. 8 minimum is 256.9 V s/m at 1940 rpm. 237 is the single-gain result of Sec. 4.

Legend: 500 rpm g=1487, 1300 rpm g=1162, 2500 rpm g=585, 3000 rpm g=797. Fig. 8 gives 1479 / 1158 / 543 / 794.5 at these speeds (1487 is the Fig. 8 maximum at 740 rpm, not the 500 rpm value). The plotted Fig. 6a peaks and Fig. 6b poles are mutually consistent and, with the 1-DOF + Eq. (3) loop at zeta=1.34 %, correspond to g ~ 1543 / 1162 / 685 / 830. Only the 1300 rpm case is consistent across legend, Fig. 8 and curves.

ambiguities.topic: Hidden part of the Fig. 9 controlled SLD
ambiguities.description: The controlled curve is one vector path sampled every 10 rpm from 500 to 3000 rpm. Opaque white rectangles drawn after it cover 1500-2050 rpm and 960-970 rpm - exactly the speeds where the controlled curve lies below the uncontrolled one. In the hidden band it falls to 3.23 mm at 1940 rpm while the uncontrolled SLD there is ~29 mm. In print the solid line seems to stop at 1500 and restart at 2050 rpm.

ambiguities.topic: Interpolated parts of the gain map
ambiguities.description: Fig. 8 has constant-slope stretches 500-550, 560-620, 620-740 (a single segment) and 1410-1860 rpm (25 collinear vertices). These look like linear interpolation rather than per-speed optima; 1410-1860 overlaps the hidden band of Fig. 9.

1.2 mm matches the uncontrolled minima (1.212 mm). No 3.6 mm minimum exists on the Fig. 9 controlled curve: the visible minimum is 3.82 mm at 2070 rpm and the hidden one 3.23 mm at 1940 rpm. The Fig. 11 single-gain minima are 3.52 mm. Model context (zeta 1.34 %): global minimum of the ZOA SLD is 3.24 mm for g=237 and 3.41 mm for g=257 (smallest Fig. 8 gain).
From the Fig. 9 curves the ratio is 12.15 at 730 rpm and peaks at 12.65 (710 rpm). '13' is a rounded value; experimentally only 8 mm (stable) was cut at 700 and 760 rpm, so the 13x is a prediction.

Sec. 4/5 say the mapped gain allows stable cutting up to 10 mm at 1300 rpm; Fig. 9 and Fig. 10 classify 1300 rpm / 10 mm as chatter (cut B), with 8 mm stable (cut A). The single-gain curve of Fig. 11 is ~5.1 mm at 1300 rpm; the single-gain tests are at 1200 rpm (3 mm stable, 4 mm chatter). The '3 mm' therefore seems to be the 1200 rpm experiment and '10 mm' the boundary bracket 8-10 mm.
Table 3 'proposed' a_lim differs from the Fig. 9 controlled curve by +0.5 mm at 1300 (12.0 vs 11.50), +0.24 at 2300, +0.26 at 2800 and +0.24 at 3000 rpm; the other rows agree within 0.1 mm.

ambiguities.topic: Worked example vs optimum at 1300 rpm
ambiguities.description: g=1240 gives a_lim=11.8 mm (text), the optimum g~1160 gives 12.0 mm (Table 3) and Fig. 9 shows 11.50 mm. A larger gain giving a smaller a_lim is possible (actuator-mode interaction) but the three numbers cannot all be on the same curve unless the a_lim(g) relation is non-monotonic near 1160-1240.
2785.6 'N/m' equals the Eq. (3) constant wp^2 (rad^2/s^2); it is not a stiffness. The beam modes of Table 1 (23, 47 Hz) are not part of the model (rigid interface).

g is in V s/m, so g*xdot is a voltage; Eq. (3) gives 3 N/V. The text writes F_d = g xdot and compares it with 27 N. Whether the check used g|xdot| (V), 3 g|xdot| (N) or the actuator output force is not stated; the worked example (29 N at g=1240, a=11.8 mm, 1300 rpm) can discriminate.

Two mapped-gain chatter points fall below the published controlled curve: 1300 rpm/10 mm (curve 11.50 mm) and 2800 rpm/5.5 mm (curve 6.34 mm). All other points are on the predicted side. The 1200/4 and 3000/4 mm single-gain chatter points lie only ~0.1 mm above the Fig. 11 curve.

The Fig. 12 caption gives no control state. From the Fig. 11 glyphs: A (+) and B (diamond) are uncontrolled cuts at 2800 rpm - the same points as the uncontrolled 2800 rpm points of Fig. 9 - while C (circle) and D (x) are single-gain controlled cuts at 2700 rpm.
Sec. 3 says uncontrolled stability was characterised at 1200 and 2800 rpm, but Fig. 9 also has an uncontrolled chatter marker at 700 rpm, 4 mm.
SADE population size, F/CR initialisation, learning period, generation cap, stagnation tolerance and the bounds of the gain search set are not given (the set is only named).

The diamond-marked line of Fig. 10 cut B is at ~149.5 Hz (raw read-out), only ~2-3 Hz below spindle harmonic 7 (151.7 Hz) which shows as a separate smaller line; digitisation resolution is ~1.24 Hz/px.
The legend's marker swatch is painted over by a white box; the legend shows only the two curve styles (cosmetic).
